notes.title: Snakebird too hard? Check out Snakebird Primer!
notes.content:
If Snakebird had you stumped try Snakebird Primer, an easier Snakebird to get you settled into every nuance of the mechanics and mold your mind into the right shape to deal with these pesky puzzles.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1014140/Snakebird_Primer/

notes.title: Patch 1.02
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/LSDU5Mb.png[/img]

[b]Change log:[/b]
[list]
[*]Better GUI scaling on high resolution screens.
[*]Can not click "through" the GUI and click a level at the same time anymore.
[*]Other minor GUI tweaks.
[*]Changed the camera so it doesn't center on a bird when clicking stuff.
[*]Undo no longer change which bird is selected.
[*]Undo shortcut on the mouse changed from Mouse4 to Mouse3 (the scroll wheel).
[*]Fruits no longer flicker when pressing Undo.
[*]Again, possibly some stuff we forgot about.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 1.01 is live!
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/LSDU5Mb.png[/img]
[b]Change log:[/b]
[list]
[*] Added remappable keys.
[*] Added a "High Quality" checkbox under Screen Settings.
[*] Removed the diagonal-move bug.
[*] Properly removed the Redo (E) command. It was never supposed to be there in the first place (hence the bugs). It may be finished up and reintroduced in the future if it's missed.
[*] Fixed a crash related to the grid.
[*] Curious George can now be completed, sorry about that. The letters on the title screen counted as something else rather than themselves. Click them again.
[*] Fixed a broken clickable (the box on level 27).
[*] The menu now displays what level you're playing.
[*] The splash screen now obeys your sound settings.
[*] Possibly a few extremely minor and forgotten changes.
[/list]

notes.title: Is It A Bird? Is It A Snake? It s Both, And A Puzzle Game
notes.content:
The ‘snake’ part of Snakebird [official site] is pretty clear: you control winding wormoids who grow and loop and get themselves into awkward situations. What does the ‘bird’ bring to the table? Does one then launch these snakebirds at castles to crush lizardpigs? Do you spin them off into oodles of licensed tie-ins and merchandise deals? (Actually, kids would probably love snakebird cuddly toys.) Nah, as far as I can tell, the ‘bird’ is simply because they have beaks and make silly bird noises. Good-o!

Snakebird’s a newly-announced puzzler by Nimbus developers Noumenon Games, which is coming out in a fortnight. Come see in a trailer.
